newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines tells IMF won't be spoiled by success.
newsitem.headline: Philippines tells IMF won't be spoiled by success.

text.p: The Philippines has told the International Monetary Fund it does not intend to be complacent despite its expected exit from IMF supervision.

"We have no illusions that our exit from the IMF signals our opportunity to relax. On the contrary, it means that we will be under tighter surveillance by the private capital markets," Finance Secretary Roberto de Ocampo said.
De Ocampo was speaking at the annual IMF and World Bank conference in Washington last week. The text of his speech was released to reporters in Manila on Saturday.
He said the Philippines welcomed scrutiny by private capital markets.

"We are ... careful to nurture hard-earned gains in securing the confidence of the financial markets that has facilitated our progress from being the 'sick (country) of Asia' to its rising star," he said.

The Philippines has a three-year extended fund facility (EFF) with the IMF which expires in June next year when the country hopes to leave the IMF-supervised programme and obtain a seal of good housekeeping.
The facility provides 474.5 million special drawing rights (SDRs), equivalent to $690 million. Manila has utilised only 36.5 million SDRs, or $53 million.
An IMF review team which visited Manila last week said the Philippines' strong economic growth would help lift the country into the ranks of fast growing industrialised economies.
